Hillel Newman, the Israeli ambassador to Australia, maintained the IDF attack on an aid convoy that killed Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom was a “reasonable mistake” and said disciplinary measures had been taken against IDF personnel involved. Newman spoke to RN Breakfast after the Australian government said it was “outraged” there would be no criminal investigation into Frankcom’s death. The ambassador said there were still legal processes in the appeal system that could be used as Israel is a “robust” democracy. We do grieve on the situation with the family. This was unintentional … and not deliberate in any way. … You know there are tragic circumstances in a war zone. And we’re very sorry for the family, but that does not always mean that there’s criminal liability.

Brisbane woman allegedly attacked and raped on morning walk A man has been charged with several counts of rape after an alleged random attack on a woman who was out on a morning walk, AAP reports. The woman, aged in her 20s, was walking in the leafy, semi-rural Brisbane suburb of Brookfield around 6.30am on Thursday when she was allegedly stopped by an unknown man, police said in a statement. The man allegedly sexually assaulted the victim multiple times before he fled the scene on foot. Police later arrested a 32-year-old man a short distance from the scene. He has been charged with six counts of rape, stalking, assault with intent to commit rape, assault occasioning bodily harm and deprivation of liberty. He is due to appear in court later today. Police said

Sydney air traffic controllers have ‘grave concerns’ about collision risk after airspace redesign Air traffic controllers at Sydney airport have warned federal safety regulators they have “grave concerns” about changes to airspace rules introduced last month, likening the situation to the months leading up to a crash in Washington DC in which 67 people died. Guardian Australia can reveal the federal government was notified on Thursday of a confidential complaint considered by the Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB), in which an experienced air traffic controller warned in June that changes related to the new Western Sydney International airport had been rushed, with “inadequate training for controllers, of all experience levels”. The complainant told the regulator a large group of controllers in Sydney “hold grave concerns about the project”, referring to the air traffic redesign to accommodate the new airport.

Sydney air traffic controllers have ‘grave concerns’ about collision risk after airspace redesign

Air traffic controllers at Sydney airport have warned federal safety regulators they have “grave concerns” about changes to airspace rules introduced last month, likening the situation to the months leading up to a crash in Washington DC in which 67 people died.

Guardian Australia can reveal the federal government was notified on Thursday of a confidential complaint considered by the Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB), in which an experienced air traffic controller warned in June that changes related to the new Western Sydney International airport had been rushed, with “inadequate training for controllers, of all experience levels”.

The complainant told the regulator a large group of controllers in Sydney “hold grave concerns about the project”, referring to the air traffic redesign to accommodate the new airport.
